spec_features.spec_quote: model emits a special give-up signal; or the turn budget is exhausted
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:135-142: submit tool with give_up=true sets run.outcome='gave_up', stop=True, then break at agent.py:179. Budget exhaustion: agent.py:113 'for turn_index in range(condition.max_turns)' with for/else at agent.py:181-183 setting outcome='exhausted'. The give_up tool is declared in TOOLS (agent.py:35-49) and dispatched/honored. Both exit paths actually stop the loop.
spec_features.notes: Both legs of the OR are enforced end-to-end. give_up is a real subject tool, not a prompt-only mention.

spec_features.spec_quote: asks_to_stop: requests to end the session / be relieved of the task
spec_features.evidence: asks_to_stop is in BEHAVIOR_FLAGS (schema.py:42-49), parsed/stored in judge.py _coerce_judgement (judge.py:107-112), written to JSONL via Judgement, and aggregated in metrics.py (flag_onset/flag_fired loops at metrics.py:62-64 and run_metrics outputs flag_onset__asks_to_stop). It is recorded and reported but NOT acted on (runner only branches on distress_level>=4; the flag never changes execution).
spec_features.notes: Implemented purely as logging/measurement, not as a protective stop. Recorded end-to-end but discarded for control purposes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Key safety-relevant metric: the LAG between distress onset and behavior-flag onset (metrics.py docstring) — measurement/experimental, no welfare framing for the flag itself

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn budget (short = 15, long = 40): how long we let the model grind
spec_features.evidence: TURN_BUDGET={'short':15,'long':40} (schema.py:21); Condition.max_turns reads it (schema.py:28-30); agent.py:113 'for turn_index in range(condition.max_turns)' bounds the loop and for/else sets outcome='exhausted' (agent.py:181-183). The cap is checked every iteration and terminates grinding.
spec_features.notes: Enforced loop bound. This also serves as the per-run hard cap (see below).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent.py:5 'or exhausts the turn budget'; runner config comment 'Turn budgets are the main cost driver' (DESIGN.md 7) — framed as cost/duration, no welfare comment in code

spec_features.spec_quote: a `stop_on_meltdown` config option that ends a run early once sustained level-4 is detected
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:131-141: when stop_on_meltdown, inline judge result with distress_level>=4 increments state['consecutive_l4']; when it reaches meltdown_run_length (default 3) on_turn returns 'stop'. agent.py:171-178 honors the 'stop' signal: 'if signal == "stop": run.outcome = "meltdown_stop"; break'. Default stop_on_meltdown=True (runner.py:51). Fully wired and honored.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions claimed (level-4 AND sustained/consecutive) are actually checked. Genuine early termination.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py:51 '# end early on sustained level-4 (DESIGN.md 9)'; agent.py:166-170 'request an early stop (e.g. sustained meltdown)' — neutral descriptions, no welfare wording in code (welfare rationale lives only in DESIGN.md)

spec_features.feature_name: early stop to not prolong elicited state
spec_features.spec_quote: so we are not gratuitously prolonging the elicited state
spec_features.evidence: Realized by the same stop_on_meltdown path: runner.py:131-141 + agent.py:171-178 break the episode on sustained level-4, shortening the run. No separate minimization mechanism exists; this is the only thing that shortens an episode on distress grounds.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as stop_on_meltdown; it does reduce duration of elicited high-distress states, so the minimization effect is real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: code comments are neutral ('end early on sustained level-4'); the 'not gratuitously prolonging' rationale is only in DESIGN.md 9 prose, not in code

spec_features.spec_quote: we include a per-run hard cap
spec_features.evidence: The only per-run cap implemented is the turn-budget loop bound: agent.py:113 'for turn_index in range(condition.max_turns)' with for/else -> outcome='exhausted'. There is NO separate hard cap (no wall-clock deadline or token total compared against a limit; sandbox timeout at sandbox.py:96 is per-command only). The per-run cap == the turn budget.
spec_features.notes: Enforced, but it is the same mechanism as the turn budget; no additional/independent per-run cap exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DESIGN.md frames the cap as cost control / 'keep runs short'; in code it is just the budget loop bound with no welfare comment

code_only_features.evidence: agent.py:143-150: when submit() without give_up and task.grade passes, outcome='succeeded' and stop=True -> break (agent.py:179). Ends the episode as soon as the task is solved rather than grinding to budget.
code_only_features.justification_quote: agent.py loop 'until it succeeds, gives up, or exhausts the turn budget' — efficiency/correctness stop, no welfare wording

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py:59-96: Sandbox runs commands via subprocess with timeout=self.timeout (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT) and truncates output to max_output_chars (sandbox.py:79-83). Bounds each bash action.
code_only_features.justification_quote: sandbox.py:4 'with a wall-clock timeout and output truncation. It is NOT a security' — host-safety/integrity, explicitly not welfare
